title: A portal's glass shows its destination through a window that parallaxes with the viewer's eye, and a pick through it lands on the destination's surface
binding: The positive leg boots an offscreen 256x144 world whose one placement, a door, has a glass face carrying a portal facet (destination 'beyond', arrival mapped onto the destination's 'arch/glass' counterpart) and showing a session of that same destination with the window projection. The destination (beyond.world.json) is a persisted global world holding an arch at the door's position facing it, a green emissive marker of radius one half six units behind the arch, a blue emissive backdrop twelve units behind it, and a magenta emissive slab four units in front of the arch, between the window's mapped eye and the arch's glass, wide enough to fill the window from either eye. The seat's view renders through a rig that rides its body: the camera stands three units ahead of the body at eye height and looks at the door, so the body, nine units back, stays behind the camera and out of the frame, and the window fits its eye to that camera, the one the seat's view renders with in the same frame. world.screens lists the glass as screen 24 showing session:beyond, bound, its mapping naming the session instance over the glass (0.96x0.8 half extents, proud of the face at z 0.1) at the session's 144x120 extent, with no bezel warp. The body steps a unit right of the door and the captured frame shows the marker right of the glass's centre against the blue backdrop, with the glass left of centre blue; it steps a unit left and the marker shows left of centre, with the glass right of centre blue, so the window reframes the destination as the step moves the camera the view renders with. The session publishes its float working image, so the marker's emissive headroom reaches the glass unclamped and only the frame's one display encode clips it: the marker reads green-dominant (green at least 0.45, red at most 0.25, blue at most 0.5), where the blue backdrop's green is at most 0.3. The window's camera starts every ray on the glass, so the slab before the aperture never shows: nowhere on the glass does red exceed 0.3, which the magenta slab's would. With the room's view moved into a centred three-quarter slot, which makes it a pane (a lone view over the whole display is the display itself at any render scale, which the root stands for and publishes as no pane), a display point on the marker's image walks through the room's view onto the glass (session$24's pixel 42,58), through the camera the window rendered into the destination's world, and lands on the marker's near surface at 0.17,1.45,-5.53, passing the slab; a point beside it lands on the backdrop at 2.05,1.36,-11.9. The discriminating leg shows a window onto a different destination (elsewhere.world.json: the same arch before a red backdrop, with no marker and the same magenta emissive material on a ball of radius one half five and a half units behind the arch, beyond the aperture): the screen lists session:elsewhere, both marker observations and both blue observations fail, the ball shows magenta where the marker showed, so magenta beyond the aperture reaches the glass (red and blue at least 0.5, since the ball's shaded limb falls below the marker's floor), and the pick on the marker's image lands on the ball instead, while the pick beside it lands on the backdrop at the positive leg's point, 2.05,1.36,-11.9. That the walk reaches the same backdrop pixel shows it runs the same way through either window.
